record.context_brief: Derivation length for one-rule string rewriting
record.original_question: For a one-rule length-preserving string-rewriting, or semi-Thue, system, what is the best upper bound on the length of a derivation as a function of the length n of the initial string and the size k of the rule?

evidence.quote: What is the best bound on the length of a derivation for a one-rule length-preserving string-rewriting system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A string-rewriting (semi-Thue) system over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ consists of a set of rewriting rules of the form $\ell 	o r$ with $\ell, r \in \Sigma^*$. A single rewriting step $u \Rightarrow v$ holds if there exist $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ and a rule $\ell 	o r$ such that $u = x\ell y$ and $v = x r y$. A derivation from a word $w_0$ is a sequence $w_0 \Rightarrow w_1 \Rightarrow \dots \Rightarrow w_m$, and its length is $m$.

Call the system length-preserving if $|\ell| = |r|$ for every rule, and one-rule if it consists of exactly one rule $\ell 	o r$. Define the size of the (unique) rule as $k = |\ell| = |r|$.

Let $D(n, k)$ denote the supremum, over all length-preserving one-rule systems whose rule has size $k$ and all starting words $w_0$ of length $n$, of the length of any terminating derivation from $w_0$.

Determine the best possible upper bound on $D(n,k)$ as a function of $n$ and $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: No closed-form best upper bound on the derivation length for arbitrary one-rule length-preserving string rewriting systems as a function of (n, k) was located in the literature. Related work (canonical automata, match-bounded systems, rational transductions for such one-rule length-preserving systems) studies structural and complexity properties but does not appear to settle a tight general bound. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: A canonical automaton for one-rule length-preserving string rewrite systems
status_evidence.snippet: Defines a letter-to-letter transducer computing the relation induced by a one-rule length-preserving system; studies structure of derivations.
status_evidence.claim: Structural analyses exist but no tight derivation-length bound is given.

status_evidence.title: One-Rule Length-Preserving Rewrite Systems and Rational Transductions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies rationality of relations induced by one-rule length-preserving rewrite systems.
status_evidence.claim: Focus is on rationality, not on tight derivation length bounds.

status_evidence.title: Match-Bounded String Rewriting Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Match-bounded systems are linearly terminating; framework for derivation length analysis of subclasses.
status_evidence.claim: General one-rule length-preserving derivation-length bound remains unaddressed.
